intent: Show that something is loading, as a small spinning glyph or, with a label, a self-contained loading block.
typical_uses: A loading indicator beside text or inside a container (a card, a table cell) that has no button of its own to carry the loading state

dont_use_when.situation: A loading state inside a Button

instead.note: Button's `loading` already centers a spinner, sets `aria-busy` and keeps the button's own accessible name; rendering this component there duplicates that wiring by hand and can double the accessibility announcement.

dont_use_when.situation: A placeholder that holds the shape of content still loading
Work whose completed fraction is known

invariants.text: On the bare shape the rendered svg defaults to `role="status"` and `aria-label="Loading"`. Both are ordinary svg props a consumer may override by passing their own `role` or `aria-label`.

Passing a `label` or a `description` that actually renders something switches the component from the bare svg to the composed block; `undefined`, `null`, `false` and `""` count as absent and leave the component on the bare shape, so a conditional such as `label={busy && 'Saving'}` does not open an empty live region when `busy` is false.

In the composed shape the outer block, not the glyph, is the live region: it defaults to `role="status"` (a consumer's own `role`, including an explicit `role={undefined}` to opt out entirely, wins over the default) and receives any `aria-live`/`aria-atomic` the consumer passes. The glyph itself is always rendered `aria-hidden="true"` and never takes the default `aria-label`; the block announces its visible label and description, not a second hardcoded "Loading". A consumer `aria-label` still lands on the hidden glyph and names nothing.
`compact` is reflected as `data-compact` on whichever element is currently the root - the bare svg, or the composed block's outer element - never on the inner indicator or glyph directly.

anti_patterns.dont: Render this inside Button by hand
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use Button's own `loading` prop - it keeps the button's width and accessible name and reports `aria-busy` while staying focusable

anti_patterns.dont: Override the default accessible name with an empty `aria-label=""`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep the default `aria-label="Loading"` or supply a real one - an empty override announces nothing to assistive tech

anti_patterns.dont: Pass both `label` and `aria-label` expecting `aria-label` to win
anti_patterns.do_instead: With a `label` the block announces its visible text; a consumer `aria-label` lands on the aria-hidden glyph and names nothing, so put the wording in `label` itself

a11y.by: spinner.test.tsx's own role/aria-label assertions on the bare shape and its role/aria-live/aria-atomic/aria-hidden and role={undefined} assertions on the composed block

label.states: label is a React node, not a string
label.because: `ReactNode` has no JSON Schema representation - a string, a number, a fragment or `false`/`null`/`undefined` (all of which count as absent, see the label-or-description-composes-the-block invariant) are all valid and only tsc can tell them apart. Its presence is what switches the component to the composed block, whose live region announces it.

description.states: description is a React node, not a string
description.because: `ReactNode`, for the same reason as `label`. It is the second line under the label, announced together with it once the block is composed.

unexposed_parts.reason: spinner.tsx renders it only in the composed shape to size and centre the glyph; it is not exported as a component of its own, so a consumer cannot reach or replace it independently - only the whole Spinner.
spinner.tsx renders it only when `label` renders something, to set the label's type; it is not exported as a component of its own, and what goes in it is the `label` prop.
spinner.tsx renders it only when `description` renders something, to set the second line's type; it is not exported as a component of its own, and what goes in it is the `description` prop.

good.title: The composed block, with a label and a second line
good.code: <Spinner label="Saving" description="This can take a minute" />

bad.title: Rendered inside Button by hand
bad.why: Button already has a `loading` prop for this: it keeps the button's width, keeps its accessible name and reports `aria-busy` while staying focusable. A hand-rolled Spinner here also opens a second live region nested inside whatever announces the button itself.

bad.title: Accessible name dropped with an empty override
bad.why: An empty `aria-label` replaces the default "Loading" with nothing, so the bare spinner announces no accessible name at all to assistive tech. Keep the default or pass a real label instead.
